lines.differs: Tougher on AtliQ than Trustline: Payment is due in 30 days instead of 45, though the total fee is significantly higher at EUR 88,000.
Same as PayTrack: Payment terms are 30 days and the structure is milestone-based, although the currency and total value differ.
Tougher on AtliQ than Rohan Iyer: AtliQ is the supplier here with milestone payments, whereas with Rohan Iyer, AtliQ was the payor for monthly timesheets.
Tougher on AtliQ than Rohan Iyer: Rheinwerk gets a perpetual license to AtliQ's PipeKit, whereas AtliQ previously secured ownership of the contractor's work product.
Broadly like Orbit Travels: AtliQ retains its proprietary PipeKit tool but must grant the client a broad, perpetual license to use it.
Same as Crestline: AtliQ retains ownership of its pre-existing PipeKit tool but grants the client a perpetual license to use it within the deliverables.
Same as Acme: Both apply a 0.5% milestone fee penalty per week of delay, capped at 5%, with exclusions for client-caused delays.
Easier for AtliQ than Brightwater: 0.5% per week capped at 5% of the milestone is much lower than 1% of total contract value per day.
Easier for AtliQ than Al Noor: Penalty is 0.5% per week with a 5% cap, whereas Al Noor required 1% per week with no cap.
Easier for AtliQ than CareBridge: Liability for slight negligence is capped at 1x total fees, whereas CareBridge was capped at 2x annual fees.
Broadly like Rohan Iyer: Both cap aggregate liability at 12 months' fees, but this clause adds specific unlimited liability for gross negligence under German law.
Broadly like PayTrack: Both cap liability at the total fees paid, but this version includes specific German law categories for unlimited liability.
Tougher on AtliQ than PayTrack: Indemnity covers any "culpable breach," whereas PayTrack limited indemnity to specific breaches like confidentiality, IP, or gross negligence.
Tougher on AtliQ than Acme: This requires indemnity for any "culpable breach," while Acme was restricted to confidentiality, IP, and gross negligence.
Tougher on AtliQ than Al Noor: Indemnity applies to any "culpable breach" of the agreement, rather than being limited specifically to IP infringement claims.
Tougher on AtliQ than Crestline: Confidentiality obligations last for 5 years after termination, compared to 3 years in the Crestline agreement.
Broadly like Al Noor: Both require standard confidentiality, but this clause specifies a 5-year post-termination survival period.
Tougher on AtliQ than Orbit Travels: Confidentiality survival is 5 years, significantly longer than the 2 years previously signed with Orbit Travels.
Broadly like Northwind: Both require a DPA and use Standard Contractual Clauses for transfers to India, but under GDPR rather than UK GDPR.
Tougher on AtliQ than Acme: Requires a formal GDPR Art. 28 DPA and EU Standard Contractual Clauses, whereas Acme only cited Indian data laws.
Easier for AtliQ than Al Noor: Uses EU Standard Contractual Clauses for data transfers to India instead of requiring prior written consent for every transfer.
Tougher on AtliQ than Brightwater: Disputes are settled in Munich under German law, shifting the risk from English law and London courts.
Tougher on AtliQ than Northwind: Replaces London-based LCIA arbitration with German law and litigation in Munich courts.
Broadly like Crestline: Both mandate local client law and courts (Germany vs. Ohio), requiring AtliQ to defend disputes in the client's home jurisdiction.
